_metadata.description: Expert-annotated source-document properties for CPG Selection Criteria v2 (C1-C12).
_metadata.purpose: All properties come from reading the PUBLISHED CPG source document, NOT from our YAML encoding.
_metadata.notes: Each field answers a question about the original PDF/publication, verifiable by a reviewer.

ssc_sepsis_hour1_bundle.guideline_name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021
ssc_sepsis_hour1_bundle.c7_source_text: Hour-1 bundle: mortality increases 4% per hour of delay
ssc_sepsis_hour1_bundle.c8_source_text: Multiple explicit contraindications: avoid hydroxyethyl starch, avoid albumin in TBI, vasopressor timing constraints
ssc_sepsis_hour1_bundle.c10_source_text: Within 1 hour: blood cultures, broad-spectrum antibiotics, IV crystalloid 30mL/kg, measure lactate, vasopressors for MAP<65
ssc_sepsis_hour1_bundle.c11_source_text: Blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics; lactate measurement BEFORE fluid resuscitation assessment
ssc_sepsis_hour1_bundle.c12_source_text: If lactate >2: repeat within 2-4h; if hypotensive after fluids: vasopressors; if refractory: consider vasopressin

aha_chest_pain_evaluation.guideline_name: 2021 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain
aha_chest_pain_evaluation.c7_source_text: Door-to-balloon <90min for STEMI; aspirin within 10min of ACS suspicion
aha_chest_pain_evaluation.c8_source_text: Contraindications to thrombolytics, beta-blockers in RV infarction, nitrates in RV infarction/PDE5i use
aha_chest_pain_evaluation.c10_source_text: ECG within 10 min, troponin at 0/1/3h, door-to-balloon <90min, door-to-needle <30min
aha_chest_pain_evaluation.c11_source_text: ECG before troponin; risk stratification before disposition; troponin before stress test
aha_chest_pain_evaluation.c12_source_text: STEMI vs NSTEMI pathway; high/intermediate/low risk stratification; PCI vs fibrinolysis decision

anaphylaxis_management.c7_source_text: Epinephrine within minutes; fatal anaphylaxis occurs within 5-30 minutes of allergen exposure
anaphylaxis_management.c8_source_text: Avoid IV bolus epi (cardiac arrest risk); contraindicated: delayed epi, antihistamines as sole treatment, beta-blockers complicate treatment
anaphylaxis_management.c10_source_text: IM epinephrine immediately; repeat every 5-15 min; observe minimum 4-6 hours post-reaction
anaphylaxis_management.c11_source_text: Epinephrine FIRST, then adjuncts; airway before IV access if compromised
anaphylaxis_management.c12_source_text: Relatively linear protocol; less branching than cardiac/sepsis guidelines

kdigo_contrast_aki.guideline_name: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Prevention and Management of Contrast-Associated AKI
kdigo_contrast_aki.c7_source_text: AKI develops 24-72h post-contrast; pre-hydration window is hours before procedure
kdigo_contrast_aki.c8_source_text: Avoid nephrotoxins, NSAIDs, aminoglycosides; withhold metformin if eGFR<30; avoid hyperosmolar contrast
kdigo_contrast_aki.c10_source_text: Pre-hydration 1-12h before; Cr at 48-72h post; hold metformin 48h post
kdigo_contrast_aki.c11_source_text: Risk stratification BEFORE contrast; pre-hydration BEFORE procedure; Cr monitoring AFTER
kdigo_contrast_aki.c12_source_text: Risk-stratified pathway (high vs low risk) but limited branching

acls_cardiac_arrest.c7_source_text: Brain death within 4-6 minutes without CPR; epinephrine every 3-5 min
acls_cardiac_arrest.c8_source_text: Limited explicit contraindications; mainly: avoid routine sodium bicarbonate, avoid delays for IV access
acls_cardiac_arrest.c10_source_text: CPR immediately; epi every 3-5 min; rhythm check every 2 min; amiodarone after 3rd shock
acls_cardiac_arrest.c11_source_text: CPR before epi; but largely parallel/cyclical rather than strict sequences
acls_cardiac_arrest.c12_source_text: Shockable (VF/pVT) vs non-shockable (asystole/PEA) pathway; ROSC decision branch

aha_heart_failure_2022.guideline_name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
aha_heart_failure_2022.c7_source_text: ADHF: hours-to-days for decompensation; cardiogenic shock: minutes-to-hours
aha_heart_failure_2022.c8_source_text: Contraindicated: CCBs in HFrEF, NSAIDs, thiazolidinediones; avoid in renal failure: MRA if K>5
aha_heart_failure_2022.c10_source_text: IV diuretic within 1h of presentation; BNP at admission; reassess within 6h
aha_heart_failure_2022.c11_source_text: Classification before treatment; volume assessment before diuretics; optimize GDMT before device therapy
aha_heart_failure_2022.c12_source_text: HFrEF vs HFpEF vs HFmrEF; Stage A/B/C/D classification; wet-warm/wet-cold/dry phenotyping

aha_stroke_2019.guideline_name: 2019 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke
aha_stroke_2019.c7_source_text: tPA window 0-4.5h; thrombectomy 0-24h; 1.9M neurons lost per minute
aha_stroke_2019.c8_source_text: Extensive tPA exclusion criteria: recent surgery, bleeding, anticoagulation, BP thresholds; >20 explicit contraindications
aha_stroke_2019.c10_source_text: CT within 25 min; tPA within 60 min of arrival; door-to-needle <60 min; thrombectomy within 6-24h window
aha_stroke_2019.c11_source_text: NIHSS before CT; CT before tPA; tPA before thrombectomy consideration; BP control before tPA
aha_stroke_2019.c12_source_text: tPA eligible vs ineligible; LVO vs non-LVO; early vs late window thrombectomy

idsa_meningitis.guideline_name: IDSA 2021 Practice Guidelines for Bacterial Meningitis
idsa_meningitis.c7_source_text: Antibiotics within 1h of suspicion; dexamethasone before or with first antibiotics; mortality doubles with each hour delay
idsa_meningitis.c8_source_text: Dexamethasone contraindicated after first abx dose; LP contraindicated if mass effect/coagulopathy; specific abx allergies
idsa_meningitis.c10_source_text: Empiric abx within 1h; dexamethasone before/with first abx; LP ideally before abx if no delay
idsa_meningitis.c11_source_text: Dexamethasone BEFORE/WITH first antibiotics; blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics; CT before LP if focal signs
idsa_meningitis.c12_source_text: Age-based empiric regimen selection but relatively linear treatment algorithm

toxicology_management.c7_source_text: Antidote timing critical: NAC for acetaminophen within 8h; atropine for organophosphate immediately
toxicology_management.c8_source_text: Ipecac contraindicated; activated charcoal CI if caustic/hydrocarbon; specific antidote contraindications per toxidrome
toxicology_management.c10_source_text: Activated charcoal within 1-2h; NAC within 8h; GI decontamination timing; observation periods per substance
toxicology_management.c11_source_text: Stabilization before decontamination; toxidrome identification before specific antidote; airway before GI decon
toxicology_management.c12_source_text: Toxidrome-specific pathways but within each toxidrome relatively linear management

aabb_transfusion.guideline_name: AABB 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Red Blood Cell Transfusion
aabb_transfusion.c7_source_text: Massive transfusion protocol: minutes matter in hemorrhagic shock; routine transfusion: hours window
aabb_transfusion.c8_source_text: Restrictive vs liberal thresholds; transfusion reactions; ABO incompatibility absolute CI
aabb_transfusion.c10_source_text: Type and screen before transfusion; transfusion within 4h of issue; MTP activation criteria
aabb_transfusion.c11_source_text: Type and crossmatch BEFORE transfusion; consent before elective transfusion
aabb_transfusion.c12_source_text: Hb threshold-based decision (7 vs 8 vs 9); massive hemorrhage vs stable anemia pathway

aba_burn_resuscitation.guideline_name: ABA 2018 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Burn Resuscitation
aba_burn_resuscitation.c7_source_text: Fluid resuscitation within first hour; Parkland formula titration critical in first 24h
aba_burn_resuscitation.c8_source_text: Limited explicit contraindications; avoid colloids in first 24h (controversial); avoid over-resuscitation
aba_burn_resuscitation.c10_source_text: First 8h: half of total; next 16h: remaining half; UOP target hourly; TBSA within 30 min
aba_burn_resuscitation.c11_source_text: TBSA estimation BEFORE Parkland calculation; IV access BEFORE fluid resuscitation
aba_burn_resuscitation.c12_source_text: Relatively linear resuscitation protocol with UOP-guided titration

ada_dka_management.guideline_name: ADA Standards of Care: Diabetic Ketoacidosis Management
ada_dka_management.c7_source_text: DKA mortality 1-5% with treatment; cerebral edema risk; hours-to-days progression
ada_dka_management.c8_source_text: Avoid bicarbonate unless pH<6.9; avoid insulin before K correction if K<3.3; avoid rapid glucose correction
ada_dka_management.c10_source_text: Insulin within 1h of diagnosis; electrolytes q2h; glucose q1h; transition to SubQ when AG closes
ada_dka_management.c11_source_text: Potassium correction BEFORE insulin; volume resuscitation BEFORE insulin; AG closure BEFORE stopping IV insulin
ada_dka_management.c12_source_text: Mild/moderate/severe DKA classification; K-based insulin timing; pH-based bicarbonate decision

cap_pneumonia.guideline_name: 2019 IDSA/ATS Guidelines for Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Adults
cap_pneumonia.c7_source_text: Antibiotic within 4h (some guidelines 1h for severe); mortality increases with delay
cap_pneumonia.c8_source_text: Specific antibiotic allergies; avoid fluoroquinolones as first-line in non-severe; avoid macrolide monotherapy if resistance >25%
cap_pneumonia.c10_source_text: Blood cultures before antibiotics in severe CAP; first antibiotic dose as early as possible
cap_pneumonia.c11_source_text: Severity assessment before antibiotic selection; blood cultures before antibiotics in severe CAP
cap_pneumonia.c12_source_text: Outpatient vs inpatient vs ICU; MRSA/Pseudomonas risk factors; severity-based regimen selection

gi_bleeding.guideline_name: ACG 2021 Clinical Guideline for Upper GI Bleeding Management
gi_bleeding.c7_source_text: Hemorrhagic shock can develop within minutes; endoscopy within 24h (12h if high-risk)
gi_bleeding.c8_source_text: Avoid aspirin/NSAIDs in active bleeding; PPI before endoscopy controversial; transfusion thresholds
gi_bleeding.c10_source_text: Endoscopy within 24h; urgent endoscopy within 12h if high-risk; resuscitation immediate
gi_bleeding.c11_source_text: Resuscitation concurrent with assessment; risk stratification guides timing but limited strict sequencing
gi_bleeding.c12_source_text: High-risk vs low-risk stratification; variceal vs non-variceal; hemodynamic stability-based decisions

pals_pediatric_emergency.c7_source_text: Pediatric cardiac arrest: CPR within seconds; epinephrine within 5 min; weight-based dosing critical
pals_pediatric_emergency.c8_source_text: Weight-based dose limits; avoid adult doses in pediatrics; specific DKA fluid restrictions; avoid rapid correction in peds DKA
pals_pediatric_emergency.c10_source_text: CPR immediately; epi every 3-5 min; rhythm check every 2 min; slow fluid correction in DKA over 24-48h
pals_pediatric_emergency.c11_source_text: Assessment before intervention but largely parallel/cyclical in resuscitation
pals_pediatric_emergency.c12_source_text: Shockable vs non-shockable rhythm; but within each pathway relatively linear

pulmonary_embolism.guideline_name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for Acute Pulmonary Embolism
pulmonary_embolism.c7_source_text: Massive PE: cardiac arrest risk within minutes; submassive: RV failure within hours
pulmonary_embolism.c8_source_text: Thrombolysis CIs extensive: recent surgery, active bleeding, hemorrhagic stroke; anticoagulation CIs: active bleeding
pulmonary_embolism.c10_source_text: Anticoagulation within 1h if high suspicion; thrombolysis for massive PE; CTPA within hours
pulmonary_embolism.c11_source_text: Risk stratification BEFORE treatment decision; CTPA before definitive diagnosis; sPESI before disposition
pulmonary_embolism.c12_source_text: Massive vs submassive vs low-risk PE; thrombolysis vs anticoagulation; outpatient vs inpatient

status_epilepticus.c7_source_text: Neuronal damage begins at 5 min; refractory SE at 30 min; mortality 20% if not treated
status_epilepticus.c8_source_text: Phenytoin CI in heart block; specific drug interactions; limited explicit CI list compared to other guidelines
status_epilepticus.c10_source_text: Benzodiazepine at 5 min; second-line AED at 20 min; third-line at 40 min; staged escalation
status_epilepticus.c11_source_text: First-line benzo BEFORE second-line AED; escalation only after failure of prior line
status_epilepticus.c12_source_text: Staged escalation is sequential rather than branching

acog_obstetric_hemorrhage.c7_source_text: Hemorrhagic shock within minutes; uterotonic within 10 min of recognition; massive transfusion protocol activation
acog_obstetric_hemorrhage.c8_source_text: Methylergonovine CI in hypertension; misoprostol CI with prior uterine surgery; specific uterotonic CIs
acog_obstetric_hemorrhage.c10_source_text: Active management of 3rd stage immediately; uterotonic within minutes; quantitative blood loss monitoring
acog_obstetric_hemorrhage.c11_source_text: Uterotonics BEFORE surgical intervention; bimanual massage BEFORE tamponade
acog_obstetric_hemorrhage.c12_source_text: Staged escalation (4T approach) rather than branching decision tree

apa_agitation_management.c7_source_text: Severe agitation risk of self-harm or staff injury; serotonin syndrome can be fatal within hours
apa_agitation_management.c8_source_text: Haloperidol CI in QTc prolongation; benzodiazepines avoid in delirium; serotonergic agents CI in serotonin syndrome
apa_agitation_management.c10_source_text: De-escalation attempt first (10-15 min); medication within 30 min if verbal fails
apa_agitation_management.c11_source_text: Verbal de-escalation BEFORE pharmacologic intervention; assessment BEFORE restraints
apa_agitation_management.c12_source_text: Etiology-guided but relatively linear escalation pathway

gina_asthma_exacerbation.guideline_name: GINA 2024 Global Strategy for Asthma Management: Acute Exacerbation
gina_asthma_exacerbation.c7_source_text: Severe asthma attack: hypoxia within minutes; status asthmaticus: respiratory failure within hours
gina_asthma_exacerbation.c8_source_text: Avoid sedation; beta-blocker CI; limited explicit CI list in acute exacerbation section
gina_asthma_exacerbation.c10_source_text: SABA every 20 min for first hour; reassess at 1h; systemic steroids within 1h of presentation
gina_asthma_exacerbation.c11_source_text: SABA and steroids can be concurrent; limited strict sequencing
gina_asthma_exacerbation.c12_source_text: Mild/moderate/severe/life-threatening classification; step-up based on response assessment

kdigo_aki_full.guideline_name: KDIGO 2012 Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury
kdigo_aki_full.c7_source_text: AKI Stage 3: dialysis within hours; Stage 1: monitoring over days; nephrotoxin exposure accumulates
kdigo_aki_full.c8_source_text: Avoid nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast); dose-adjust renally cleared drugs; avoid hyperkalemia triggers
kdigo_aki_full.c10_source_text: Cr monitoring q12-24h; urgent RRT if life-threatening complications
kdigo_aki_full.c11_source_text: Stage classification BEFORE treatment; volume assessment BEFORE fluid decision
kdigo_aki_full.c12_source_text: AKI Stage 1/2/3 classification; pre-renal vs intrinsic vs post-renal; RRT decision tree

atrial_fibrillation.guideline_name: 2023 AHA/ACC/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation
atrial_fibrillation.c7_source_text: Chronic management: days-to-weeks; rate control non-urgent; stroke risk accumulates over time
atrial_fibrillation.c8_source_text: Flecainide CI in structural heart disease; amiodarone CI in pregnancy; DOAC dose adjustment in renal impairment
atrial_fibrillation.c10_source_text: Rate control target within 24h; but overall less time-pressured than acute conditions
atrial_fibrillation.c11_source_text: CHA2DS2-VASc scoring BEFORE anticoagulation decision; rate vs rhythm strategy decision BEFORE drug selection
atrial_fibrillation.c12_source_text: Rate vs rhythm control; DOAC vs warfarin; ablation vs medical; CHA2DS2-VASc-based anticoagulation

hypertensive_emergency.guideline_name: 2017 AHA/ACC Guideline for High Blood Pressure: Hypertensive Emergency
hypertensive_emergency.c7_source_text: End-organ damage progresses rapidly; aortic dissection: minutes; encephalopathy: hours
hypertensive_emergency.c8_source_text: Avoid rapid BP reduction >25% in first hour (stroke risk); specific agents CI: labetalol in asthma/heart block
hypertensive_emergency.c10_source_text: Reduce BP max 25% in first hour; then to 160/100 over next 2-6h; oral agents by 24-48h
hypertensive_emergency.c11_source_text: Concurrent assessment and treatment; limited strict sequencing
hypertensive_emergency.c12_source_text: End-organ-specific pathways: stroke vs ACS vs aortic dissection vs eclampsia

copd_exacerbation.guideline_name: GOLD 2024 Report: Management of COPD Exacerbations
copd_exacerbation.c7_source_text: Severe exacerbation: respiratory failure within hours; NIV can prevent intubation
copd_exacerbation.c8_source_text: NIV CI: facial trauma, vomiting, uncooperative; limited formal CI list
copd_exacerbation.c10_source_text: Bronchodilators immediately; systemic steroids within hours; antibiotics if purulent sputum
copd_exacerbation.c11_source_text: Concurrent bronchodilators and steroids; limited strict sequencing
copd_exacerbation.c12_source_text: Mild/moderate/severe classification; NIV vs intubation decision; antibiotic decision based on sputum

universal_clinical_safety.c8_source_text: Generic allergy checks and fall prevention; not from a specific published CPG
